gaps: ENT-17 (`ai_model_source`, `ai_conversation`, owner system-setting) has no org/project scoping, no cost-cap/quota fields, and no `ai_conversation_message` table — CR-H01's turn-level storage and per-org/per-project model config are not yet modeled in the KG.
No KG element for BL-J02 (hide AI nav button when AI off) exists yet — referenced in the request but unverifiable in this snapshot.
No business rule or entity defines AI cost-cap/quota semantics (reset period, hard-stop vs warn) needed for AC-AI-04.
No AI-specific retry/backoff rule exists; closest precedents (ADR-10 retry-3-with-backoff, FR-JIR-07 RETRYABLE/BLOCKED/FAILED classification) are for Jira/queue sync, not outbound LLM calls.
conflicts: CR-H01's proposed routes (`/ai/conversation/{add,chat,update,list,delete,chat/list}`) do not match FR-SYS-07's currently traced API surface (`POST /system/ai-config/save`, `GET /system/ai-config/list`, `POST /personal/model/edit-source`, `POST /functional/case/ai/chat`, `POST /functional/case/ai/transform`) — the spec's API field and traceability need reconciling or FR-SYS-07 needs a revision.

BRL-64 (shared by FR-SYS-07, FR-SYS-09, FR-AUT-09, FR-CAS-13, FR-REV-05, FR-PLN-12, FR-API-14, FR-MCP-02, FR-UI-04) and ADR-12 mandate deferred features be fully hidden (404 + `X-Route-Missing: 1`), never 501/200-fake; ADR-12 itself records the AI 501 as a tracked exception (OI-02). AC-AI-05's 503-when-`AI_ENABLED=false` is a third status code pattern not covered by BRL-64/ADR-12 or by the staged-rollout flag convention in NFR-MA-05 (`report`→`on`), so it should be confirmed as an intentional, distinct convention for 'built but administratively off' features.

options.title: Phased AI platform: add aiclient + chat routes under AI_ENABLED, leave transform/legacy ai-config endpoints untouched
options.summary: Build shared/pkg/aiclient and the AIService (ResolveModel/ListMessages/AppendTurn) with new ai_conversation_message table and new /ai/conversation/* routes, gated by AI_ENABLED (503 when off). Extend ENT-17's AiModelSource with org/project scoping, encrypted API key, and cost/quota fields, but explicitly keep `/system/ai-config/*`, `/personal/model/edit-source`, and `/functional/case/ai/transform` as-is (still 501 per original FR-SYS-07) until CR-H02.
options.approach:
- Add `shared/pkg/aiclient`: OpenAI-compatible HTTP client, 60s timeout, 2 retries honoring `Retry-After`, reuse `shared/pkg/netguard` (ADR-15/NFR-SE-05) under the `AdminTarget` profile for outbound SSRF protection, OTel metrics per ADR-13/NFR-OB-02, secret masking in logs/metrics per NFR-SE-04.
- Extend ENT-17's `ai_model_source` with org/project foreign keys, cost-limit/quota fields, and encrypted `app_key` using the existing AES-256-GCM/`secretbox` pattern from BRL-46/BRL-46-style constraint (never return plaintext, mask on read — same as FR-SYS-03's LDAP secret pattern).
- Add `ai_conversation_message` table; implement `AIService.ResolveModel/ListMessages/AppendTurn`.
- Mount `/ai/conversation/{add,chat,update,list,delete,chat/list}` behind `AI_ENABLED`; return 503 on all of them when the flag is off (distinct, documented exception to the BRL-64/ADR-12 404 deferred-feature pattern since AI is now implemented, just togglable).
- Leave `/functional/case/ai/transform`, `/system/ai-config/*`, `/personal/model/edit-source` untouched (still 501 under current FR-SYS-07 wording) — scoped explicitly out, to be revisited with CR-H02.
- Enforce org quota check before any provider call (reject with clear message, no outbound call) for AC-AI-04.
pros: Reuses the centralized SSRF guard mandated by ADR-15/NFR-SE-05 instead of inventing a second blocking mechanism, satisfying AC-AI-07 with an already-reviewed control.
Follows the established secret-masking convention from BRL-46/NFR-SE-04/FR-SYS-03 for API keys, directly satisfying AC-AI-03 with precedent the review has already accepted.

Resolves the long-tracked 501 exception noted in ADR-12 (OI-02) without touching the other FRs that share BRL-64 (FR-SYS-09, FR-AUT-09, FR-CAS-13, FR-REV-05, FR-PLN-12, FR-API-14, FR-MCP-02, FR-UI-04), keeping their deferred-feature guarantees intact.
Smaller, additive diff: no existing route is retired, lowering regression risk against FR-SYS-07's currently documented API/UC-16/UC-38 traceability.
cons: Leaves FR-SYS-07 partially inconsistent: the FR still documents `/functional/case/ai/transform` and `/system/ai-config/*` as part of its API, but this option doesn't implement or formally re-scope them, so the SRS/traceability (FR-SYS-07) will read as half-done until a follow-up revision.
Introduces a 503-on-disabled convention that has no precedent entity/rule (gap vs. BRL-64/ADR-12's 404 pattern and NFR-MA-05's report→on flag model) and needs an explicit decision record.
Org/project cost-cap and quota fields are new schema on ENT-17 with no existing entity/rule to model against, so the quota semantics for AC-AI-04 must be designed from scratch.

risks.description: Spec drift: FR-SYS-07's API/acceptance text becomes inaccurate without a companion SRS revision
Quota/cost-cap enforcement logic (AC-AI-04) has no existing pattern to copy and could under- or over-block legitimate calls if designed late
Provider key handling bugs could leak secrets through logs/metrics despite NFR-SE-04 intent if masking isn't applied at every boundary (API, log, span)

options.rollback: Set AI_ENABLED=false (routes return 503); revert the migration adding ai_conversation_message and the org/project/cost columns on ai_model_source since no other code path depends on them yet.

options.title: Full replacement: retire legacy ai-config/transform endpoints and rewrite FR-SYS-07's API surface in one release
options.summary: Replace FR-SYS-07's entire documented API (`/system/ai-config/*`, `/personal/model/edit-source`, `/functional/case/ai/transform`) with the new `/ai/conversation/*` routes plus new org/project model-config endpoints in a single CR, retiring the old ones and updating the SRS/FR-SYS-07 definition to match immediately.
options.approach:
- Implement aiclient and AIService as in Option 1.
- Additionally design and ship new `/system/ai-config/*`-equivalent org/project configuration endpoints, then remove/redirect the old `/system/ai-config/save`, `/system/ai-config/list`, `/personal/model/edit-source`, `/functional/case/ai/transform` routes.
- Update FR-SYS-07's statement, API, and acceptance fields in the same change so the SRS stays consistent with shipped behavior (closing the conflict noted above instead of deferring it).
- Migrate any existing `ai_model_source`/`ai_conversation` rows to the new org/project-scoped schema.
pros: Closes the FR-SYS-07 API/route conflict immediately instead of leaving it for a later revision — SRS and shipped behavior stay in sync.
Single coherent API surface for AI configuration (no legacy `/system/ai-config/*` vs new `/ai/conversation/*` split) simplifies future CR-H02 work on test-case generation.
Still reuses ADR-15/NFR-SE-05 (netguard) and BRL-46/NFR-SE-04 (secret masking) exactly as in Option 1 for AC-AI-07/AC-AI-03.
cons: Retiring `/functional/case/ai/transform` and `/system/ai-config/*` is explicitly broader than the CR-H01 body's route list, risking scope creep beyond what's described (CR says transform/ai-config generation is out of scope via CR-H02).
Breaking change for any existing caller/UI wired to `/system/ai-config/*` or `/personal/model/edit-source`, requiring coordinated UI/MCP updates beyond what CR-H01 lists.
Larger migration surface increases the chance of violating ADR-16-style caution ('tránh xoá dữ liệu') if old `ai_model_source` rows aren't carefully preserved during schema change.

risks.description: Retiring endpoints not explicitly scoped in the CR could break untracked internal/UI callers
Combined schema migration + route cutover increases blast radius and rollback complexity versus an additive approach

affected_areas.name: AI configuration screens depending on legacy endpoints

options.rollback: Requires redeploying the prior release with legacy routes restored and reversing the schema migration; harder than Option 1 because old endpoints are removed, not just left dormant.

options.title: Minimal spike: ship aiclient + mock-ext/one real provider chat path, defer org/project cost-cap and quota enforcement
options.summary: Deliver the smallest slice that satisfies most ACs fast — aiclient, AIService, chat routes, AI_ENABLED flag, SSRF guard, secret masking — but skip per-org/project cost-limit and quota tracking, deferring AC-AI-04 to a quick follow-up once usage data exists.
options.approach:
- Same aiclient/AIService/chat-route work as Option 1, minus org/project cost-cap and quota fields on ENT-17.
- `AI_ENABLED` flag and 503 behavior still implemented for AC-AI-05.
- netguard (ADR-15) and secret masking (BRL-46/NFR-SE-04) still included since they're required by AC-AI-03/AC-AI-07 and cheap to reuse.
- AC-AI-04 is explicitly left unimplemented in this slice; a follow-up CR adds quota/cost-cap once real usage/cost data from mock-ext and the first approved provider is available.
pros: Fastest path to a working chat loop (AC-AI-01/AC-AI-02/AC-AI-05/AC-AI-06/AC-AI-07/AC-AI-03 all achievable) without needing to invent quota semantics upfront.
Still reuses ADR-15/NFR-SE-05 and BRL-46/NFR-SE-04 patterns, so no security shortcuts are taken even though scope is trimmed.
Reduces the risk called out for Option 1/2 around designing cost-cap logic without data — ships it later with real usage numbers.
cons: Does not satisfy AC-AI-04 at release — an explicit acceptance criterion in the CR is left unmet, which the CR as written does not allow as 'ngoài phạm vi'.
Risk of unbounded provider spend between this release and the deferred quota follow-up, since no cap mechanism exists yet.
Still leaves the FR-SYS-07 API-surface conflict and the BRL-64/503 convention question open, same as Option 1.

risks.description: Shipping AI chat without any cost cap exposes the org to unbounded provider billing before the follow-up CR lands
CR explicitly lists AC-AI-04 as acceptance; descoping it may not be acceptable to stakeholders without an explicit amendment

options.rollback: Set AI_ENABLED=false; revert the ai_conversation_message migration since nothing else depends on it.

options.title: Model org/project AI config as an instance of the existing generic service-config entity (ENT-18) instead of a bespoke schema
options.summary: Reuse ENT-18's existing per-organization service-configuration pattern (organization_id, global, config_schema — already used for plugin/integration config under FR-SYS-09) to carry AI model-source, API key, and cost/quota data per org/project, rather than growing ENT-17 with ad-hoc columns.
options.approach:
- Implement aiclient/AIService/routes as in Option 1.
- Instead of adding org/project/cost columns directly onto `ai_model_source`, store org/project-scoped overrides and cost/quota settings as a `config_schema` JSON payload under ENT-18's generic organization-service-config table, with `ai_model_source` holding only the provider-agnostic defaults.
- Encrypt the API key field inside the JSON payload using the same AES-256-GCM/secretbox mechanism as BRL-46, masked on read.
- Netguard (ADR-15) and AI_ENABLED/503 behavior unchanged from Option 1.
pros: Avoids introducing a second org/project-scoping mechanism alongside the one ENT-18 already provides for FR-SYS-09-style per-org service configuration — one less new pattern for reviewers to validate.
Keeps `ai_model_source` (ENT-17) stable and close to its current shape, reducing migration risk on an existing table.
Still satisfies AC-AI-01/02/03/05/06/07 the same way as Option 1 via the same aiclient/netguard/secret-masking reuse.
cons: ENT-18's `config_schema` is JSON/schema-less by design (used for deferred plugin config per FR-SYS-09), which makes querying/enforcing structured cost-cap and quota rules (AC-AI-04) harder than first-class typed columns — likely needs an additional typed usage/quota table regardless.

Conflates a currently 'always-off, deferred' entity (ENT-18 is tied to FR-SYS-09, which is explicitly hidden per BRL-64/v4 'chưa có runtime plugin') with a now-active AI feature, which may confuse ownership and the deferred-feature guarantees FR-SYS-09 relies on.
Less direct mapping to the CR's explicit `ai_model_source`/org/project wording, requiring more design negotiation before implementation starts.

risks.description: Reusing a deferred-feature entity (ENT-18/FR-SYS-09) for an active feature could blur the BRL-64 'fully hidden' guarantee if not carefully isolated
JSON config_schema makes atomic quota decrement / enforcement under AC-AI-04 more error-prone than typed columns

options.rollback: Set AI_ENABLED=false; drop the new ai_conversation_message table and the AI-specific ENT-18 config rows, leaving FR-SYS-09's existing (deferred) use of ENT-18 untouched.

recommendation.reason: It satisfies all seven ACs with the smallest, additive diff, reuses the two security patterns the KG already mandates (netguard SSRF profiles per ADR-15/NFR-SE-05, and AES-256-GCM secret masking per BRL-46/NFR-SE-04) instead of inventing new ones, and avoids retiring or rewriting the parts of FR-SYS-07's API surface (transform, legacy ai-config) that the CR explicitly places out of scope — leaving that reconciliation for a deliberate follow-up rather than bundling it into a risky single release.

assumptions.text: `/functional/case/ai/transform`, `/system/ai-config/*`, and `/personal/model/edit-source` remain untouched (still 501 under FR-SYS-07) after CR-H01 ships, pending CR-H02.
AI_ENABLED's 503-when-off behavior is an intentional, documented exception to the BRL-64/ADR-12 404 deferred-feature convention, since the feature is implemented but administratively toggled off.
The mock-ext OpenAI-compatible provider referenced in AC-AI-01 is a test double already available in the environment, not something this CR must build from scratch.

open_questions.text: Which existing FR-SYS-07 API endpoints (`/system/ai-config/*`, `/personal/model/edit-source`, `/functional/case/ai/transform`) are retired, kept as-is, or re-scoped by CR-H01, and does FR-SYS-07's SRS/URD text get revised in this change or a follow-up?
Should org/project AI model configuration live on a dedicated extension of ENT-17 (`ai_model_source`) or reuse the generic per-org service-config entity ENT-18 already used for FR-SYS-09?
What are the exact cost-cap/quota semantics for AC-AI-04 (hard stop vs. soft warning, reset period, per-org vs per-project granularity), since no existing entity or business rule defines this today?
Is BL-J02 (hide AI nav button when AI is off) tracked anywhere reviewable, since it has no corresponding element in the current knowledge-graph snapshot?

requirement_coverage.note: Core chat+list flow via new AIService/routes in all options.
Depends on at least one approved real provider being configured; aiclient design is provider-agnostic across options.
All options reuse BRL-46/NFR-SE-04 masking pattern for API keys.
Org/project cost-cap and quota enforcement implemented before shipping; opt-3 explicitly defers this.
Minimal spike ships without quota/cost-cap; deferred to a follow-up CR.
AI_ENABLED flag gates all /ai/conversation/* routes with 503 in every option.
aiclient retry/Retry-After logic is shared across all options.
All options route outbound calls through shared/pkg/netguard per ADR-15/NFR-SE-05.
